title: Outlook: admin policy for "Days of email to save" in new Outlook for Windows offline settings
summary: The briefing accurately reports the planned policy and distinguishes it from the existing offline-access switch. The undocumented policy details remain open after targeted searches; minor corrections concern source citations and an omitted navigation heading.

claims.claim: The cited sync-window change appears under May 30, 2025, version 20250523006.11.
The default offline mail sync window was expanded from seven days to 30 days.
claims.quote: Offline Days of email to save expanded to 30 days: The default mail sync window in offline mode has been expanded from seven days to 30 days.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Days of email to save controls how many days of email are saved locally for offline access.
claims.quote:
Select the number of days to save emails locally:
1. Select Settings > General > Offline > Days of email to save.
2. From the dropdown, select 7, 30 (this is the default value), 90, or 180 days of email to save.
claims.fix: Add https://support.microsoft.com/office/2460e4a8-16c7-47fc-b204-b1549275aac9, titled 'How to work offline in Outlook for Windows', to sources for the existing local-save behaviour.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes an offline mail setting, not a new sign-in or permission path.

claims.claim: Microsoft warns that raising classic Outlook's SyncWindowSetting through GPO triggers full OST resynchronisation and can affect bandwidth across many clients.
claims.quote: When GPO changes SyncWindowSetting to any higher value, Outlook will do a full OST resynchronization when the new value applies. For a single client, this is not problematic. Applying a higher value to hundreds or more clients at the same time could adversely affect available network bandwidth.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated that the planned new Outlook policy triggers the full resynchronisation described for classic Outlook.
claims.quote: Searched: new Outlook Days of email to save admin policy default values PowerShell Cloud Policy Intune; offline settings Days of email to save licensing price meter policy. Read classic sync-window article, Policy Management and release notes; no such mechanism is stated for this policy.

claims.quote: To use the Outlook for Windows desktop app (either the classic or new version) with a Microsoft 365 organizational email address, you need to purchase a plan that includes the desktop versions of the Microsoft 365 apps.

claims.claim: Most new Outlook mailbox policies apply to both Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows, rather than being independently enabled for each client.
claims.quote: Most of the mailbox policies apply to both Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows, so you can't enable them on one client but not the other.
claims.fix: Keep the cited 'most' wording, but note that https://learn.microsoft.com/exchange/clients-and-mobile-in-exchange-online/outlook-on-the-web/outlook-web-app-mailbox-policies states 'All mailbox policies set for Outlook on the web will also affect new Outlook for Windows'; cite that page alongside the existing source.

claims.claim: The Exchange admin center route to the mailbox policy's Offline access section is Roles > Outlook web app policies > policy > Manage access > Offline access.
claims.quote:
In the EAC, go to Roles > Outlook web app policies.
Access: Select Manage access. In the Edit access flyout that opens, the available settings are visible in the following sections:
- File access
- Offline access
claims.fix: Change controls[1].ui.path and the rendered path to 'Roles > Outlook web app policies > policy > Access > Manage access > Offline access'. Access is the omitted heading; the cited page documents the route only as far as the Offline access section.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: existing-control table row
claims.claim: Set-OwaMailboxPolicy -OfflineEnabledWin $false disables new Outlook for Windows offline capabilities.
claims.quote: The OfflineEnabledWin parameter specifies whether offline capabilities are available in Outlook (formerly known as the new Outlook for Windows), including saving items to the local device (view items without an internet connection).

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: OfflineEnabledWin controls whether new Outlook can be used offline, not the number of days of mail to save.
claims.quote:
$true: Users can manage offline capabilities in Outlook. This value is the default.
$false: Users can't manage offline capabilities in Outlook. No items are saved to the user's device. Previously save items are deleted.

claims.claim: The existing mailbox-policy control can govern a group of users.
claims.quote: A mailbox can only have one Outlook on the web mailbox policy applied to it. You can create different policies for different types of users in your Exchange Online organization.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/exchange/clients-and-mobile-in-exchange-online/outlook-on-the-web/outlook-web-app-mailbox-policies to sources for mailbox-policy scope; this is the same source addition requested for the cross-client documentation difference.
